canonical_statement: The study aimed to determine whether CBD was helpful for improving sleep and/or anxiety in a clinical population and also examined tolerability, safety, and patient acceptance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This study aimed to determine whether CBD is helpful for improving sleep and/ or anxiety in a clinical population. Given the novel nature of this treatment, our study also focused on tolerability and safety concerns.

canonical_statement: The investigators conducted a retrospective chart review of adult psychiatric outpatients treated with CBD for anxiety or sleep as an adjunct to treatment as usual.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A retrospective chart review was conducted of adult psychiatric patients treated with CBD for anxiety or sleep as an adjunct to treatment as usual at a large psychiatric outpatient clinic.

canonical_statement: Case-series inclusion required a clinician-diagnosed sleep or anxiety disorder, consent to CBD treatment for one of those disorders, and at least 1 month of active CBD treatment with follow-up.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Selection for the case series was contingent on informed consent to be treated with CBD for 1 of these 2 disorders and at least 1 month of active treatment with CBD.

population.label: Potential adult psychiatric outpatients
inclusion_criteria: At least 1 month of active CBD treatment with follow-up

canonical_statement: Patients with sole or primary diagnoses of schizophrenia, posttraumatic stress disorder, or agitated depression were excluded from the final case-series sampling frame.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with sole or primary diagnoses of schizophrenia, posttraumatic stress disorder, and agitated depression were excluded.

population.label: Sampling frame
exclusion_criteria: Sole or primary posttraumatic stress disorder

canonical_statement: The sampling frame consisted of 103 adults consecutively treated with CBD at the psychiatric outpatient clinic.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The sampling frame consisted of 103 adult patients who were consecutively treated with CBD at our psychiatric outpatient clinic.

population.label: Adults consecutively treated with CBD

canonical_statement: The final sample consisted of 72 adults: 47 with primary anxiety concerns and 25 with primary poor-sleep concerns, each with at least one follow-up visit after CBD was prescribed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The final sample consisted of 72 adult patients presenting with primary concerns of anxiety (65.3%; n = 47) or poor sleep (34.7%; n = 25) and who had at least 1 follow-up visit after CBD was prescribed.

population.label: Final analytic cohort: primary anxiety or poor sleep

canonical_statement: Nearly all patients received oral CBD 25 mg/day in capsule form; dosing was generally morning for predominant anxiety and evening for predominant sleep complaints, with a minority receiving 50 or 75 mg/day and one patient titrated to 175 mg/day.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Nearly all patients were given CBD 25 mg/d in capsule form. If anxiety complaints predominated, the dosing was every morning, after breakfast. If sleep complaints predominated, the dosing was every evening, after dinner.

exposures.details: Capsule; generally morning for anxiety and evening for sleep; minority received 50 or 75 mg/day and one patient was titrated to 175 mg/day.

canonical_statement: Anxiety was monitored monthly with the 14-item Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A), scored from 0 to 56.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale is a widely used and validated anxiety measure with 14 individual questions. It was first used in 1959 and covers a wide range of anxiety-related concerns. The score ranges from 0 to 56.

canonical_statement: Sleep was monitored monthly with the Pittsburg Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), a 19-item self-report measure scored from 0 to 21, with higher scores indicating more sleep-related concerns.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The Pittsburg Sleep Quality Index is a self-report measure that assesses the quality of sleep during a 1-month period. It consists of 19 items that have been found to be reliable and valid in the assessment of a range of sleep-related problems.

outcome.definition: 19-item self-report sleep quality measure; higher scores indicate more sleep-related concerns

canonical_statement: Side effects and CBD tolerability were assessed through spontaneous patient self-reports documented in case records.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Side effects and tolerability of CBD treatment were assessed through spontaneous patient self-reports and were documented in case records.

canonical_statement: Deidentified patient data were analyzed with descriptive statistics and plotted for visual interpretation of trends; no inferential comparative analysis was reported.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Deidentified patient data were evaluated using descriptive statistics and plotted graphically for visual analysis and interpretation of trends.

canonical_statement: The authors reported a more sustained response in anxiety than in sleep over time, with anxiety scores decreasing within the first month and remaining lower during follow-up.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: These results demonstrated a more sustained response to anxiety than for sleep over time.

canonical_statement: The study was naturalistic and open-label with no comparison group, so efficacy could not be established from the observed changes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: These results must be interpreted cautiously because this was a naturalistic study, all patients were receiving open-label treatment, and there was no comparison group.

canonical_statement: Most patients were taking psychiatric medications and receiving other mental health services, limiting causal attribution of symptom changes to CBD.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Most patients were also taking psychiatric medications and receiving other mental health services, such as counseling, which limits the ability to make any causal links to CBD treatment.

canonical_statement: The clinical population was younger than the clinic population overall, and the authors identified possible selection bias in who chose this treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the clinical population in this case series is skewed younger than typical for our clinic, and future studies could explore the possible selection bias inherent in this treatment option.

canonical_statement: The authors noted that societal notoriety around cannabis and medical marijuana could contribute to an unusually large placebo or expectancy effect.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the large societal notoriety about cannabis and medical marijuana probably contributes to a larger-than-normal placebo effect.

canonical_statement: Clinical attrition was substantial and its relationship to CBD ingestion was unclear because reasons for later loss to follow-up were largely unknown.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Clinical attrition is evident in the dataset. The reason for this might be related to CBD ingestion or not, so the overall component remains unclear.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that CBD showed promise for reducing anxiety but emphasized that the open-label, nonrandomized case series required very cautious interpretation and that randomized controlled trials were needed for definitive guidance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: CBD displays promise as a tool for reducing anxiety in clinical populations, but given the open-label and nonrandomized nature of this large case series, all results must be interpreted very cautiously. Randomized and controlled trials are needed to provide definitive clinical guidance.
